subject.title: fix(sessions): ignore invalid saved timestamps during session recovery

question: Should OpenClaw treat historically loose-but-Date.parse-accepted persisted timestamp strings as malformed metadata, or preserve them through an explicit doctor migration before enforcing strict runtime parsing?
rationale: The code and tests support either operational model, but the repository policy makes persisted-state compatibility and fallback behavior a maintainer product decision rather than an implementation convenience.

options.title: Accept strict canonical timestamps
options.body: Merge the patch and treat non-RFC3339 persisted strings as missing metadata, preserving only canonical writer output.

options.title: Migrate known legacy values
options.body: Pause merge until a narrowly scoped doctor migration converts demonstrably shipped loose timestamp forms into canonical values before the runtime reads them strictly.

recommendation.title: Accept strict canonical timestamps
recommendation.body: Merge the patch and treat non-RFC3339 persisted strings as missing metadata, preserving only canonical writer output.

likelyOwner.reason: A current-main history pass is needed to identify the accountable session persistence owner for this compatibility decision.
